news.summary: Even a Democratic administration may struggle to reverse tariffs that help finance Trump's tax cuts.
news.body: Even a Democratic administration may struggle to reverse tariffs that help finance Trump's tax cuts. Markets hardly blinked at the announcement of a new series of proposed tariff schedules from United States President Donald Trump's administration on November 25. Although the affected economies - including the European Union, China, Japan, Indonesia and Taiwan - account for more than 53 percent of US goods trade, the announcement was met with something of a whimper. On November 25, the S&P 500 and the benchmark 10-year Treasury bond hardly moved. Compare that with the turmoil that followed Trump's April 2, 2025, "Liberation Day" announcements. news.summary: January WTI crude oil (CLF27) closed down -0.60 (-0.72%) on Friday, and January RBOB gasoline (RBF27) closed up +0.0066 (+0.27%).
news.body: January WTI crude oil (CLF27) closed down -0.60 (-0.72%) on Friday, and January RBOB gasoline (RBF27) closed up +0.0066 (+0.27%). Crude oil and gasoline prices gave up an early advance on Friday and settled mixed. Dollar strength on Friday weighed on energy prices. Also, the outlook for higher OPEC crude production is weighing on prices after Iraq's oil minister said his country is negotiating with OPEC to raise the country's crude production ceiling. Crude prices initially moved higher Friday as escalating attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised supply concerns.
